title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — jest charge: rather lose a hundred jokes than abuse Scripture
pass_a_gloss: GAR treats the John 8:58 turn as mockery—jest or earnest, let others judge. He would rather bury a hundred jokes than twist even a syllable of Scripture.
pass_b_english: GAR. Answer 1. From the words of our Lord and God, Hebrew commas—whether you expose others to mockery in jest or in earnest—let others' judgment be. I would rather lose a hundred jokes for myself than be willing to abuse even a little word of sacred Scripture.
source_text: GAR. Resp. 1. Ex verbis Domini & Dei nostri, commata Hebrae, ut alios ludibrio exponas, an sit iocus, an sit serio, aliorum iudicium esto. Malim ego sane perire mihi centum iocos, quam ut vel sacrae Scripturae verbulo abuti velim.

choices.choice: GAR: rather lose jokes than abuse Scripture word
